# `package require` provider-selection oracle — a fixed seed corpus.
#
# Captured from real interpreters, byte-identical on both:
#   tclsh8.6  (Tcl 8.6.14)
#   tclsh9.0  (Tcl 9.0.4)
#
# Each trial registers every listed version as a `package ifneeded widget V …`
# in a fresh child interpreter (in the listed order), optionally issues
# `package prefer`, then runs the listed `package require` and records the
# version that actually loaded — `ERROR` when the require failed.
#
# Generated by (transcript preserved so a reviewer can re-run it):
#
#   proc trial {prefer providers reqargs} {
#       set i [interp create]
#       $i eval [list set providers $providers]
#       $i eval [list set reqargs $reqargs]
#       $i eval [list set prefer $prefer]
#       $i eval {
#           if {$prefer ne ""} { package prefer $prefer }
#           foreach v $providers { package ifneeded widget $v [list package provide widget $v] }
#           set rc [catch {package require {*}$reqargs} res]
#       }
#       set rc [$i eval {set rc}]
#       set res [$i eval {set res}]
#       interp delete $i
#       set p [expr {$prefer eq "" ? "default" : $prefer}]
#       puts "select\t$p\t$providers\t$reqargs\t[if {$rc} {set _ ERROR} else {set _ $res}]"
#   }
#
# Row format (tab-separated):
#   select  PREFER  AVAILABLE-VERSIONS  REQUIRE-ARGS  LOADED-VERSION|ERROR
#
# `PREFER` is `default` when no `package prefer` was issued; a bare
# `package prefer` answers `stable` on both interpreters, so `default` and
# `stable` rows must agree.
select	default	1.5 2.3	widget	2.3
